guideContent.strategyOverview:
Broodfire Hatchery is a Naya combat deck built on one engine. Atla Palani, Nest Tender pays {2} and taps to make a 0/1 Egg token, and whenever an Egg you control dies she reveals cards from the top of your library until she hits a creature card and puts it straight onto the battlefield. The 99 is stocked with bodies that win a combat the moment they arrive — Worldspine Wurm, Blightsteel Colossus, Apex Altisaur, Zacama, Primal Calamity, Avacyn, Angel of Hope, Etali, Primal Conqueror, Ghalta and Mavren, Raph & Mikey, Troublemakers — so a random flip is never a blank. The play pattern is the one the board asked for: a big creature enters, big creatures attack.

Speed comes from free sacrifice outlets. Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar and Goblin Bombardment kill an Egg for no mana, Skullclamp does it for {1} and draws two cards, and High Market does it once a turn from a land slot. Maskwood Nexus makes every creature you control every creature type — so every creature is an Egg and any outlet becomes a repeatable "sacrifice a creature, hatch a new one" engine. Thornbite Staff gives Atla "whenever a creature dies, untap this creature", so with Ashnod's Altar the loop is mana-neutral and hatches the library; with a haste source on the battlefield, everything it hatches attacks the same turn. Because Atla is a Shaman, the Staff attaches to her for free if it is already on the battlefield when she enters.

Haste is the hinge. Rhythm of the Wild gives every nontoken creature riot, Samut, Hazoret's Champion gives the team haste for two mana, Rising of the Day does the same on an enchantment and gives the deck's 14 legendary creatures +1/+0, Palani's Hatcher gives Dinosaurs haste (every creature, under Maskwood Nexus), and Xenagos, God of Revels hands one creature haste and +X/+X where X is its power at each of your beginning-of-combat steps. Xenagos chooses its target when the trigger goes on the stack, so hatch in main phase 1 to use it that combat. Without a haste source, hatch at instant speed on the end step before your turn: Seedborn Muse untaps Atla during every opponent's untap step, so the Eggs are there and the bombs are ready when your turn starts.

The amplifiers turn one hatch into several attack steps. Aurelia, the Warleader, Combat Celebrant and Tifa, Martial Artist each untap every creature you control — Atla included, so she makes another Egg mid-turn — and add a combat phase; Aggravated Assault does the same for {3}{R}{R} as often as you can pay, at sorcery speed. Raph & Mikey hatch a creature tapped and attacking every time they attack. Raphael, the Nightwatcher gives every attacking creature double strike. Zopandrel, Hunger Dominus doubles the team's power and toughness at every combat, yours and each opponent's, and doubles again in each extra combat. Annie Joins Up makes every legendary creature's triggered ability trigger twice — Atla hatches two creatures per Egg, Aurelia and Tifa each add two combats, Zopandrel doubles twice, Xenagos fires twice — and Roaming Throne (naming Shaman) stacks on top. Mondrak, Glory Dominus and Elspeth, Storm Slayer double every Egg token, and Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines doubles the enters-the-battlefield triggers of Craterhoof Behemoth, Palani's Hatcher, Etali and Apex Altisaur while blanking every opponent's.

Support is built for a creature deck that taps out on its own turn: 9 ramp sources for a turn-3 Atla, 3 tutors (Worldly Tutor puts the next hatch on top of the library; Enlightened Tutor finds Rhythm of the Wild, Rising of the Day, Annie Joins Up, Aggravated Assault, Maskwood Nexus or an Altar; Natural Order finds a bomb and can sacrifice an Egg as its cost, which also hatches), 7 draw pieces tied to the hatches, and 5 protection pieces (Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver are free with the commander out; Vigor and Avacyn carry the hatched board through damage-based and destroy-based wipes). Interaction is chosen for hoser coverage: Grafdigger's Cage stops creature cards in libraries from entering the battlefield and blanks Atla outright, so Aura Shards answers it every time a creature enters, and Krosan Grip, Force of Vigor, Boseiju, Who Endures and Beast Within cover artifacts, enchantments and lands. Winds of Abandon overloaded exiles every creature the deck's opponents control before an alpha strike. Bracket 4 with 7 Game Changers. The deck is tagged brewing until the goldfish simulation confirms the turn-6 kill rate.

deckCategories.name: The Egg Engine
deckCategories.description: Atla turns Egg deaths into free creatures, so the deck's real mana sink is making more Eggs and untapping her. Maskwood Nexus makes every creature an Egg, Thornbite Staff untaps Atla on every death, Mondrak and Elspeth, Storm Slayer each double every Egg token (with both out one activation makes four), Annie Joins Up and Roaming Throne (naming Shaman) each make Atla's hatch trigger fire an additional time, Seedborn Muse untaps her on every opponent's turn, Palani's Hatcher and Nesting Dragon add Eggs without spending Atla's tap, and Elesh Norn doubles the enters-the-battlefield triggers the hatched creatures cause.

deckCategories.name: Free Sacrifice Outlets
deckCategories.description: An Egg is worth nothing until it dies. Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar and Goblin Bombardment cost no mana and have no limit, so an Egg made this turn hatches this turn and a board full of Eggs empties at instant speed — including on the end step before your turn, when the hatched bombs need no haste. Skullclamp kills an Egg for {1} and draws two; High Market does it once a turn from a land slot; Natural Order can sacrifice an Egg as its additional cost.

deckCategories.name: Haste
deckCategories.description: A hatched bomb without haste waits a turn, so the deck runs three team-wide sources plus a targeted one. Rhythm of the Wild gives every nontoken creature riot (haste or a +1/+1 counter, your choice per creature), Samut, Hazoret's Champion is a 2-mana anthem Atla can hatch, Rising of the Day is the same anthem on an enchantment and gives the 14 legendary creatures +1/+0, Palani's Hatcher gives Dinosaurs haste (every creature under Maskwood Nexus), and Xenagos, God of Revels hands one creature haste and doubles its power at each of your beginning-of-combat steps — hatch in main phase 1, because Xenagos picks its target when the trigger goes on the stack. Lightning Greaves protects Atla and lets her make an Egg the turn she lands.

deckCategories.name: Extra Combats and Untaps
deckCategories.description: Each of these turns one hatch into two or three attack steps. Aurelia (first attack each turn), Combat Celebrant (exert) and Tifa (a power-7-or-more creature connects, first combat only) untap every creature you control — Atla included, so she makes a fresh Egg between combats — and add a combat phase. Aggravated Assault adds a combat for {3}{R}{R} at sorcery speed with no limit per turn. Raph & Mikey hatch a creature tapped and attacking every time they attack, so every extra combat is another hatch. Annie Joins Up doubles the Aurelia, Tifa and Raph & Mikey triggers. Note: Tifa's extra combat has no main phase between combats, so hatches between them must be instant-speed.

deckCategories.name: Power Multipliers
deckCategories.description: Zopandrel doubles the team's power and toughness at every combat (yours and each opponent's) and doubles again in each extra combat. Xenagos doubles one creature at each beginning of combat; resolve Zopandrel first, then Xenagos, and Worldspine Wurm attacks as a 60/60; Raphael, the Nightwatcher gives every attacking creature double strike, so that Wurm deals 60 twice. Raphael is a creature, so Atla can hatch him (his sneak cost returns an unblocked attacker to hand, which is only worth it with a token). Craterhoof Behemoth is the mass finisher and has haste of its own. Ghalta and Mavren add a tapped-and-attacking X/X trampler on every attack, X being the greatest power among the other attackers. Garruk's Uprising gives the whole team trample so the doubled power goes through blockers.

deckCategories.name: Bombs to Hatch
deckCategories.description: The library is the deck's hand. Every creature here wins a combat, sweeps, or draws the game open on arrival, so a blind flip off Atla is always worth the Egg. Eight of them have printed power 7 or more, which turns on Tifa. Worldspine Wurm and Vigor shuffle back from the graveyard and become fuel again; Blightsteel Colossus with Xenagos is 22 infect trample, lethal to one player in a single hit.
cards: Etali, Primal Conqueror // Etali, Primal Sickness

deckCategories.name: Tutors
deckCategories.description: Three tutors, each with a job: Worldly Tutor puts a creature on top of the library, which is exactly where Atla's next hatch comes from; Enlightened Tutor finds Rhythm of the Wild, Rising of the Day, Annie Joins Up, Aggravated Assault, Maskwood Nexus, Thornbite Staff or either Altar; Natural Order sacrifices an Egg (which hatches) and puts Craterhoof, Vigor, Worldspine Wurm or Zopandrel onto the battlefield.

deckCategories.name: Protection
deckCategories.description: The deck taps out on its own turn with the commander on the battlefield, so every protection piece is chosen to be live then. Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver cost nothing while Atla is out, Lightning Greaves gives Atla shroud, and Vigor and Avacyn make the hatched board survive damage-based and destroy-based wipes. Clever Concealment was traded for a third haste anthem at DEC-935.

deckCategories.name: Interaction and Hoser Coverage
deckCategories.description: Grafdigger's Cage is the card that beats this deck outright — creature cards in libraries can't enter the battlefield, so Atla stops hatching. Aura Shards destroys an artifact or enchantment every time a creature enters, and Krosan Grip, Force of Vigor, Boseiju and Beast Within cover artifacts, enchantments and lands so no resolved hoser sticks. Swords to Plowshares and Path to Exile answer blockers and opposing commanders at instant speed, Annie Joins Up deals 5 to a creature or planeswalker on entry, and Winds of Abandon overloaded exiles every creature your opponents control before an alpha strike while the Egg board stays put.

deckCategories.name: Ramp and Fixing
deckCategories.description: Atla wants to land on turn 3 and activate the same turn, so the ramp is cheap and untapped: the Nature's Lore class fetches shock duals untapped, Rootbound Crag is the 37th land (untapped with any Mountain or Forest on the battlefield), and Jeska's Will pays for an Aggravated Assault activation or a whole hatch turn.

deckCategories.name: Card Advantage
deckCategories.description: Draw is tied to the plan rather than bolted on: Guardian Project and Garruk's Uprising fire on the creatures Atla hatches, Vaultborn Tyrant draws for every power-4-or-more body that enters, Skullclamp turns a 0/1 Egg into two cards, Greater Good cashes a doomed bomb in for a hand, and Caretaker's Talent draws the first time tokens enter under your control each turn — with Smothering Tithe that is every turn of the cycle. The hatch itself is the deck's real card advantage: every Egg is a free creature.

deckCategories.name: Key Lands
deckCategories.description: 37 lands, 36 of them untapped on arrival. Command Beacon recasts Atla past commander tax, High Market is a sacrifice outlet in a land slot, Boseiju is removal that costs no card, and Eiganjo channels from hand for 4 damage to an attacking or blocking creature ({1} cheaper per legendary creature you control — 14 in the deck).

winConditions.title: Hatch and Swing
cards: Etali, Primal Conqueror // Etali, Primal Sickness
winConditions.description: Kill Eggs in main phase 1, the hatched bombs have haste (Rhythm of the Wild, Samut, or Xenagos on the biggest one), and they attack. Zopandrel doubles the team at the start of combat; Xenagos doubles one body on top of that, so a hatched Worldspine Wurm attacks as a 60/60 trampler and Blightsteel Colossus as 22 infect; Raphael, the Nightwatcher gives every attacker double strike on top. Craterhoof Behemoth finishes a wide board.

winConditions.title: Extra Combat Chain
winConditions.description: Aurelia, Combat Celebrant and Tifa untap every creature you control, Atla included, and add a combat phase; Aggravated Assault adds more for {3}{R}{R} each. Between combats Atla makes a fresh Egg, a free outlet kills it, and the new bomb attacks in the next combat. Raph & Mikey hatch another creature tapped and attacking on every attack, and Annie Joins Up doubles every one of these legendary triggers.

winConditions.title: Thornbite Hatch Engine
winConditions.description: Equip Thornbite Staff to Atla. Pay {2},{T} for an Egg, sacrifice it to Ashnod's Altar for {C}{C}, and the death untaps Atla via the Staff. Each mana-neutral loop hatches a creature off the top of the library; with a haste anthem out the whole library attacks that turn.

synergies.title: Maskwood Nexus + Ashnod's Altar = dump the library for mana
synergies.description: Maskwood Nexus makes every creature you control every creature type, so every creature you control is an Egg. Sacrifice any creature to Ashnod's Altar for {C}{C}; the Egg death triggers Atla, which puts the next creature card off the top of your library onto the battlefield; sacrifice that one too. Each iteration nets {C}{C}, so you can run through the library and finish with a huge mana pool. Any converter on the battlefield turns the chain into lethal damage. Verified line: https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/240-643-2034/

sources.name: Commander Spellbook — Maskwood Nexus + Ashnod's Altar
sources.detail: Maskwood makes every creature an Egg; each sac hatches.

synergies.title: Maskwood Nexus + Phyrexian Altar = dump the library for colored mana
synergies.description: The same line on the colored-mana altar: with Maskwood Nexus out, every creature is an Egg, so each sacrifice to Phyrexian Altar adds one mana of any color and hatches the next creature. Worth running alongside the Ashnod's version because the colored mana casts whatever the chain reveals. Verified line: https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/240-643-4050/

sources.name: Commander Spellbook — Maskwood Nexus + Phyrexian Altar
sources.detail: Same line on the colored-mana altar.

synergies.title: Maskwood Nexus + Goblin Bombardment = dump the library and burn the table
synergies.description: With Maskwood Nexus out, Goblin Bombardment sacrifices any creature for one damage and each death hatches the next creature off the library. The chain is its own win condition — no separate converter needed — because every iteration pings a player for 1 while the board grows. Verified line: https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/240-643-5147/

sources.name: Commander Spellbook — Maskwood Nexus + Goblin Bombardment
sources.detail: Same line converting each sac into 1 damage.

synergies.title: Thornbite Staff + Ashnod's Altar = mana-neutral repeat hatching
synergies.description: Equip Thornbite Staff to Atla (free if the Staff is already out when she enters, since she is a Shaman). Pay {2} and tap Atla for a 0/1 Egg, sacrifice the Egg to Ashnod's Altar for {C}{C}, and the death untaps Atla through the Staff. Net mana zero, one hatch per loop, and it is fully deterministic — no Maskwood Nexus required. Verified line: https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/240-2034-2178/ With Rhythm of the Wild or Samut on the battlefield, everything the loop hatches attacks the same turn.

sources.name: Commander Spellbook — Thornbite Staff + Ashnod's Altar
sources.detail: Mana-neutral repeat hatches; see Thornbite Hatch Engine.

synergies.title: Atla + Annie Joins Up = two hatches per Egg
synergies.description: Atla is a legendary creature, so Annie Joins Up makes her dies trigger fire twice: every Egg death reveals until a creature card twice and puts both onto the battlefield. No Maskwood Nexus or Roaming Throne needed; with Roaming Throne naming Shaman as well, each Egg hatches three creatures (each "additional time" adds one).

synergies.title: Aurelia / Combat Celebrant / Tifa untap Atla mid-turn
synergies.description: All three untap every creature you control (Celebrant: every other creature) when they add a combat phase, and Atla is a creature. Pay {2}, tap her for a new Egg, kill it with a free outlet, and the bomb it hatches attacks in the extra combat with haste from Rhythm of the Wild or Samut. Tifa's extra combat has no main phase in between, so this has to happen at instant speed.

synergies.title: Raph & Mikey + extra combats = a hatch every attack
synergies.description: Raph & Mikey reveal until a creature card and put it onto the battlefield tapped and attacking whenever they attack, so each extra combat from Aurelia, Tifa, Combat Celebrant or Aggravated Assault is one more hatch that swings immediately. The hatched creature was not declared as an attacker, so attack triggers do not fire for it, but it deals combat damage like any other attacker.

synergies.title: Zopandrel + Xenagos on one body = 60 trample
synergies.description: Both trigger at the beginning of your combat. Order Zopandrel to resolve first: Worldspine Wurm becomes 30/30, then Xenagos gives it +30/+30 and haste (X is calculated as the Xenagos trigger resolves). Blightsteel Colossus on the same line is 44 infect trample. Xenagos must target a creature already on the battlefield, so hatch the target in main phase 1. With Raphael, the Nightwatcher on the battlefield the Wurm deals that damage twice.

synergies.title: Palani's Hatcher + Maskwood Nexus = every creature has haste
synergies.description: Palani's Hatcher gives other Dinosaurs you control haste. Maskwood Nexus makes every creature you control every creature type, so every hatched bomb is a Dinosaur with haste. The Hatcher's own beginning-of-combat Egg sacrifice also hatches a creature before attackers are declared.

highlights.name: Atla Palani, Nest Tender
highlights.reason: Commander. {2}, {T} makes a 0/1 Egg; whenever an Egg you control dies she reveals cards until she hits a creature card and puts it onto the battlefield. Every line in the deck is a way to kill Eggs faster and attack with what hatches.

highlights.name: Rhythm of the Wild
highlights.reason: Riot for every nontoken creature you control, which covers every hatch: the bomb enters with haste (or a +1/+1 counter if it already has haste) and attacks the turn it arrives. Creature spells can't be countered.

highlights.name: Samut, Hazoret's Champion
highlights.reason: {1}{R} 2/2: creatures you control have haste. The cheapest team-wide haste in the colours, and a creature, so Atla can hatch her.

highlights.name: Rising of the Day
highlights.reason: {2}{R} enchantment: creatures you control have haste, legendary creatures +1/+0 (14 in the deck, Atla included). The third team-wide haste source, on the permanent type that survives a wipe.

highlights.name: Xenagos, God of Revels
highlights.reason: At each of your beginning-of-combat steps another target creature gains haste and +X/+X where X is its power. Indestructible enchantment (a creature only at devotion 7). Hatch in main phase 1: the target is chosen when the trigger goes on the stack.

highlights.name: Zopandrel, Hunger Dominus
highlights.reason: Hatchable 4/6 reach that doubles the power and toughness of every creature you control at the beginning of each combat — yours and each opponent's — and again in every extra combat. Resolve it before Xenagos: 15 → 30 → 60.

highlights.name: Annie Joins Up
highlights.reason: Legendary enchantment: 5 damage to a creature or planeswalker on entry, then every legendary creature's triggered ability triggers an additional time. Atla hatches two creatures per Egg, Aurelia and Tifa each add two combats, Raph & Mikey hatch twice per attack, Zopandrel doubles twice.

highlights.name: Aurelia, the Warleader
highlights.reason: Hatchable 3/4 flying vigilance haste. The first time she attacks each turn, untap all creatures you control (Atla included, so she makes another Egg) and add a combat phase.

highlights.name: Tifa, Martial Artist
highlights.reason: Whenever one or more creatures you control with power 7 or greater deal combat damage to a player, untap all your creatures, and in the first combat of your turn add a combat phase. Eight bombs in the deck have printed power 7 or more; Zopandrel and Xenagos lift the rest.

highlights.name: Raph & Mikey, Troublemakers
highlights.reason: 7/7 trample haste. Whenever they attack, reveal until a creature card and put it onto the battlefield tapped and attacking — Atla's hatch on an attack trigger, once per combat, doubled by Annie Joins Up and (under Maskwood Nexus) by Roaming Throne.

highlights.name: Aggravated Assault
highlights.reason: {3}{R}{R}: untap all creatures you control and add a combat phase and a main phase, as often as you can pay. The repeatable extra combat on an enchantment; Enlightened Tutor finds it.

highlights.name: Raphael, the Nightwatcher
highlights.reason: {2}{R}{R} 2/3: attacking creatures you control have double strike. Hatchable, unlike an enchantment anthem; a Zopandrel-and-Xenagos Worldspine Wurm deals 60 twice.

highlights.name: Maskwood Nexus
highlights.reason: Makes every creature you control every creature type, so every creature is an Egg (any free outlet hatches the library) and every creature is a Dinosaur (Palani's Hatcher gives them all haste).

highlights.name: Thornbite Staff
highlights.reason: Gives Atla "whenever a creature dies, untap this creature". With Ashnod's Altar the hatch loop is mana-neutral. Attaches to Atla for free because she is a Shaman.

highlights.name: Ashnod's Altar
highlights.reason: Free outlet that pays you {C}{C} per Egg. The mana half of the Thornbite loop and the outlet that lets a whole board hatch at instant speed on the end step before your turn.

highlights.name: Roaming Throne
highlights.reason: Name Shaman and Atla's death trigger fires twice — two flips per Egg. The single biggest multiplier on the engine.

highlights.name: Seedborn Muse
highlights.reason: Game Changer. Untaps Atla during every opponent's untap step: an Egg per player per turn cycle (×3 in a four-player game) and the reason the deck can hatch on the end step before its turn with no haste source at all.

highlights.name: Natural Order
highlights.reason: Game Changer. Sacrifice a green Egg — which itself triggers Atla — and put Craterhoof Behemoth, Zopandrel, Vigor or Worldspine Wurm straight onto the battlefield.

highlights.name: Craterhoof Behemoth
highlights.reason: The mass finisher, with haste of its own. Any board built by a turn of hatches becomes lethal the moment Craterhoof arrives, hard-cast or flipped; Elesh Norn doubles its trigger.

highlights.name: Worldspine Wurm
highlights.reason: 15/15 trample that shuffles itself back into the library from anywhere, so it is permanent fuel for the Thornbite loop, and it leaves three 5/5 trample tokens behind each time it dies. The best Xenagos target in the deck: 30/30, or 60/60 after Zopandrel.
